metric.why: Headline queue figures now run to hundreds of gigawatts in a single grid region, but most requests are speculative and duplicated across sites. The realization gap between queued and energized megawatts is the single best measure of how much of the announced buildout is real.
metric.metric: Approval to energize versus queued load
metric.target: Read grid operator planning reports for both numbers together; either alone misleads.
metric.definition: The share of an interconnection queue that has cleared study and holds final approval to draw power, as opposed to sitting as a request. Queue totals count paper; approval to energize counts electricity.

reading.body:
Approval to energize measures the share of a grid interconnection queue that has cleared study and holds final approval to draw power, as distinct from a queued request that has not, and the data source notes that queue totals now run to hundreds of gigawatts in a single grid region because most requests are speculative and duplicated across sites.

The gap between queued and energized megawatts is described as the single best measure of how much of an announced data center buildout is actually real, which makes it a corrective to headline capacity announcements that count paper commitments rather than approved, physical grid connections. ERCOT is named as the source for reading these figures, and the guidance is to read queued and energized numbers together, since either alone misleads.

This metric sits in a cluster with capacity market clearing price, behind-the-meter generation, interconnection queue position and wait, and power purchase agreements, all tracked under Power and Grid, which together describe the different ways a facility actually secures usable electricity rather than merely announcing intent to build.
